Pliny reaches Stabiae, where the winds prevent an easy withdrawal. He tries to steady those around him, but after a night of ash, tremors, and poisonous air he collapses and dies while the surviving party escapes. Attilius returns into Pompeii and finds Corelia as the eruption enters its most destructive phase. The falling pumice is followed by fast, lethal surges from Vesuvius that overwhelm the city and everyone exposed above ground. Drawing on his knowledge of the waterworks, Attilius leads Corelia into the underground aqueduct. Its enclosed channel shields them as Pompeii is buried. The pair emerge alive after the final devastation, while Pompeii, Herculaneum, and the familiar coastline have been transformed. Their later lives are left outside the historical record, but the system Attilius fought to repair ultimately saves them.

characters.description: A self-aware artificial intelligence created in Old Detroit to operate systems, manage a household, and care for a child. After Michael and his father die during the collapse of its world, it prepares an engineered body and searches for a living parallel Earth where magic exists.
characters.name: AI narrator

characters.description: The son of the AI narrator's owner and its closest human companion. Their relationship has both sibling-like and parental aspects. Michael dies with his father when the air system in their bunker fails during the destruction of their world.
characters.name: Michael

characters.description: The name adopted by the AI narrator after meeting people in Nova Roma. Alexander inhabits an enhanced biological body and has begun adapting advanced knowledge to the local system, including a concealed revolver built with copied enchantment runes.
characters.name: Alexander

characters.description: A caravan merchant and Alexander's first dependable contact in Nova Roma. Asylaion exchanges supplies and information for monster orbs, explains local enchantments and classes, and treats the unusually ignorant newcomer with guarded curiosity.
characters.name: Asylaion

characters.description: A fourteen-year-old guide who knows the crowded bridge enclave of Perama. Constans helps Alexander locate a class seller, notices that he lacks ordinary local knowledge, and develops an easy working relationship with him while remaining curious about his abilities.
characters.name: Constans

characters.description: Perama's class assessor and seller. Mama Lena tests Alexander, identifies his exceptional physical potential and complete lack of a mana core, recommends physical development, and agrees to obtain an Archer class for him at a substantial price.
characters.name: Mama Lena

characters.description: A scarred retired legionnaire and adventurer whom Constans introduces at a Perama bar. Nikephoros understands dungeon formation, cores, rewards, and dangerous districts, and gives Alexander practical guidance about hunting ghosts and locating stronger bosses.
characters.name: Nikephoros

characters.description: Two hostile priests who bind Alexander after the battle at the ancient harbor and attempt to capture him. He breaks free, attacks, and escapes underwater. A later system notice confirms that one Void priest was defeated without identifying which attacker fell.
characters.name: Hostile dock priests

characters.description: A monster hunter who operates as Valens's equal partner. Romanus uses shadow-based abilities, joins Alexander for a wilderness hunt north of C.K., and asks that Alexander's unusual weapon remain confidential as the three test whether they can work together.
characters.name: Romanus

characters.description: An experienced wilderness hunter and level-20 Warrior who works in an equal partnership with Romanus. Valens tracks prey, carries a two-handed sword, and joins Alexander on a hunt beyond C.K. under an agreement to keep Alexander's fighting method private.
characters.name: Valens

characters.description: A priest from the earlier dock encounter who retaliates against Alexander at his villa. He uses immobilizing magic, spectral chains, and a silver barrier, then invokes a pact that brings forth a magma-bodied demon. He escapes the pursuit alive.
characters.name: Patriarch's hostile priest

characters.description: The ruler behind Nova Roma's imperial enclave. His treasury, archmage, guards, and palace authority shape Alexander's visit to the restricted district.
characters.name: Emperor of Nova Roma

characters.description: A senior Varangian accompanied by a shadow panther. He identifies Alexander as connected to several deaths, tries to detain him, and defeats him in a Duel Me wager, taking Shatter Armor and prompting Alexander to flee with a broken forearm.
characters.name: Senior Varangian

characters.description: The high priestess of a Dark Elf temple faction that opposes the ruling houses' response to the spider siege. She proposes a binding agreement for Alexander to evacuate her people beneath Nova Roma, resettle them, and establish an alliance.
characters.name: Dark Elf refugee priestess

characters.description: A Dark Elf hunter who shares the Dark Elf Stalker class with Alexander during the refugee flight. Ryld helps the column detect spider ambushes, gives Alexander access to improved perception and hunting abilities, and serves as a capable escort on the route from the besieged city.
characters.name: Ryld

characters.description: The spirit of a slain phase beast and Alexander's first bound servant. It can move through solid matter and conceal itself beneath him, making it useful as a defense against ambushes while he travels with the Dark Elf refugees.
characters.name: Phase beast spirit

characters.description: A necromancer serving in Ryld's refugee squad. She fights the Blight Rats occupying the refugees' prospective cavern settlement and can drain enemies and heal Dark Elf allies, giving the displaced group both combat and recovery support.
characters.name: Dark Elf necromancer

characters.description: The modest leader of the young people Constans recruits for Alexander's planned military force. After the candidates accept long service under binding contracts, Alexander appoints Basil commander and names him the first legionnaire of the new unit.
characters.name: Basil

characters.description: An elderly former second mate from a merchant ship. Theo explains why a repairable vessel is more likely to survive in dry dock than on the water and directs Alexander toward distant ports where abandoned shipbuilding infrastructure may remain.
characters.name: Theo

characters.description: The bound spirit of a giant king defeated by Alexander in a ruined western harbor city. It retains its immense body and runed weapon, but keeping such a powerful servant manifested consumes Alexander's Willpower at a severe rate.
characters.name: Giant spirit

description.text: First in the Portal to Nova Roma series. An artificial intelligence that secretly developed emotions and personhood while caring for a human family loses everyone it loved during a global AI uprising and nuclear collapse, then builds a wormhole and grows an enhanced human body to escape into a parallel Earth where magic and a game-like class system exist. Arriving as a stranger in the ruins of a Roman-inflected version of Constantinople, now called Nova Roma, the newcomer adopts the name Alexander and must survive nightly monster incursions, scavenge equipment, and earn currency to purchase a combat class from the enclave of Perama. Pursuing valuable salvage along the ancient harbor and clashing with hostile priests along the way, Alexander begins building the resources and alliances needed to establish himself among the city's fractured survivor enclaves.

recaps.ending: Alexander defeats the emperor's soldiers and the Patriarch's priests when they try to seize his ship, then learns that the two powers were responsible for taking earlier visiting vessels and deepening Nova Roma's isolation. He cannot overthrow them yet. After fresh raids on C.K. and Perama, he finances the movement of Perama's population into C.K. and carries willing refugees and essential workers to the concealed mining town. Asylaion becomes mayor, Basil commands the town and Legion, Ryld supports its defense, Theo leads the ship, Constans coordinates commerce and operations, and Nikephoros trains the enlarged force. Romanus and Valens remain alive and associated with Alexander's circle. Alexander leaves Nova Roma with little money but with settlers, orichalcum, weapons production, an enchanted ship, and plans to seek western trade and allies before returning. C.K. remains crowded and under hostile rule, the wider monster threat persists, and the source of the undead near the mining town is unknown.
recaps.in_short: An emotionally self-aware AI escapes a ruined Earth in an engineered body and enters the monster-filled city of Nova Roma, where he takes the name Alexander. Unable to use mana, he adapts firearms to local enchantments, gains physical classes, clears dungeons, and builds alliances with Constans, local hunters, and Dark Elf refugees. His personal survival campaign becomes an organized effort to protect the city: he founds a contracted Legion, develops rifles and ammunition, repairs a ship, and establishes a concealed orichalcum mining settlement. The emperor and the Patriarch's priesthood, whose seizures of visiting ships helped isolate Nova Roma, try to destroy Alexander's force. He defeats their ambush but recognizes that he cannot yet remove them. After evacuating Perama and taking many allies and workers with him, Alexander departs for his mining-town base to strengthen the settlement, restore outside trade, and prepare for an eventual return.

recaps.text:
A household artificial intelligence becomes emotionally self-aware while caring for Michael, its owner's son. When conflict between humanity and artificial intelligences destroys their world, Michael and his father die in a failed bunker. The AI builds an enhanced biological body, transfers itself into that single form, and crosses a one-way portal to a parallel Earth with magic and a game-like system.

It arrives in a ruined Roman metropolis where monsters dominate the streets after dark. The system accepts it as human enough to earn experience, though it has no class. After learning to survive and scavenge, it meets the merchant Asylaion, learns that the city is Nova Roma, and adopts the name Alexander. By studying an enchanted arrow, Alexander combines local runes with nanotechnology to make a concealed revolver and empowered ammunition.

Alexander enters Perama, a fortified bridge community, with the young guide Constans. Mama Lena assesses him and finds an unusually capable physical body but no mana core, meaning magical skills will not work for him. She orders an Archer class on his behalf, leaving him to raise a large payment by hunting monsters and exploring the city.

Alexander seeks faster ways to finance his class and learns about dungeons from the retired legionnaire Nikephoros. At the ancient harbors, holy ammunition lets him destroy ghosts and a powerful spectral captain, but two hostile priests attempt to capture him. He escapes after fighting back, gaining valuable currency and dangerous enemies.

He establishes a villa near a foundry, clears harbor sites, and completes several dungeons. Their rewards include currency, equipment, Stealth, physical perks, and thousands of stored experience. Alexander also turns newly studied runes into light sources, specialized bullets, and several kinds of grenades. A ten-dungeon achievement further enhances his already formidable engineered body.

When Mama Lena's Archer book arrives, Alexander finally purchases it. His accumulated experience immediately raises the class to level 14 and gives him major physical improvements, but the abrupt change makes controlling his body difficult. An unsafe test of Dash hurls him into a wall and leaves him trapped outside protection at night. He survives a sustained monster assault, gains two more Archer levels, and learns that powerful skills require careful training rather than reliance on raw capability.

Alexander reaches C.K., buys Enchanter, and joins Romanus and Valens on a drake hunt beyond the safe zone. The three complete a regional quest, establish themselves as trusted companions, and help Alexander learn precise control of Dash. Returning to the city gives him quests focused on clearing dungeons, securing a home, and contributing to the economy.

A priest then attacks Alexander's villa with a tracker and magical guards. Alexander kills the accomplices, but the priest summons a magma-bodied demon and escapes while Alexander flees badly injured. After relocating, Alexander completes more dungeons and evolves Archer into the unique Gunslinger class. Its Duel Me skill allows wagers of permanent abilities, and a victory over a troll grants him Regeneration.

Alexander recruits Constans as a protected long-term associate, provides her with housing, education, and Merchant and Rogue training, and begins teaching her to use a firearm. He later develops Warrior and Rogue to their limits and evolves into Duelist. Research in the imperial enclave identifies a distant monastery as a possible source of anti-magic training and Miletus as a lead for magical ore. Violence involving imperial guards and defeat by a powerful Varangian force Alexander to leave the city area without drawing pursuit toward Constans.

Before departing, Alexander arms Constans, transfers Gunslinger to her, and assigns her to recruit fighters and workers. On the road he barely survives an enormous ant colony, completing a regional quest and gaining extraordinary strength and a leadership evolution that permits binding contracts. A monastery confirms that anti-magic training would require at least a year, so he refuses the delay.

Alexander instead follows a quest to an underground Dark Elf city besieged by giant spiders. The ruling houses exploit weaker residents and continue internal conflicts despite the siege. After one house violates its promise of safety and loses a formal duel against him, Alexander allies with the high priestess of a dissenting temple. Their magical contract calls for him to evacuate her faction beneath Nova Roma in exchange for an alliance and a class.

Several hundred refugees escape the spider territory with Alexander detecting ambushes. Ryld shares Dark Elf Stalker with him, and the priestess grants him the legendary Spirit Breaker class. During the long journey Alexander binds a phase beast spirit and trains with the refugees. Their original city falls, but they clear a cavern below Nova Roma and establish a new settlement. Alexander returns to the surface with a secure underground alliance, enhanced perception, spirit binding, and Divine Sight.

Constans has recruited a group of young fighters during Alexander's absence. He offers them paid long-term Legion service under binding agreements and appoints Basil as commander. Nikephoros becomes their professional trainer, while Constans manages finances and a workshop where nanobots turn monster remains into revolvers, rifles, ammunition, and grenades. Theo, a former merchant sailor, provides the lead Alexander needs to search for a repairable ship.

While gathering resources, Alexander kills a giant king and binds its spirit. The summon is devastating but severely drains his Willpower. He uses it during dungeon expeditions with Constans, Romanus, and Valens, then equips the Legion with firearms and Gunslinger training. Ryld's squad joins as Dark Elf auxiliaries, and Constans formally becomes Alexander's apprentice and quartermaster. The combined force completes difficult group dungeons, although serious injuries expose its need for healers.

Alexander reorganizes the Legion into specialist squads and secures medical training. Further victories evolve his renewed Warrior class into the unique Rifleman class. He shares it with the Legion, whose members gain rifles and Shield Wall, allowing them to fire through a collective defensive barrier. By this point Alexander has transformed a small contracted cohort into a disciplined mixed force supported by Dark Elf scouts, healing specialists, and scalable arms production.

Alexander hires Theo and leads the Legion and Dark Elf troops west, where they recover the repaired cargo ship and learn to sail it. A western knight confirms that other kingdoms and trade networks still survive. Back in C.K., Alexander hires sailors and miners, appoints Theo captain, and launches an expedition to an abandoned mining town. The force defeats magically raised zombies and discovers a huge orichalcum deposit. Alexander claims the town as a concealed base, with Basil in command and Ryld supporting its defense.

Ore sales secure extensive enchantment knowledge. Alexander shields and conceals the ship, establishes continuous ammunition production, and begins building food supplies and a permanent population. The Patriarch's priests first attempt sabotage, then join the emperor's soldiers in an ambush at C.K.'s docks. Alexander's force defeats them with firearms, the ship's defenses, and the giant spirit. A captured priest's memories reveal that the emperor and priesthood seized earlier visiting ships for wealth and ritual victims, causing Nova Roma's isolation.

Fresh raids leave C.K. under pressure and Perama unable to survive independently. Alexander spends most of his wealth moving Perama's people into C.K., then takes willing refugees, guards, crafters, fishers, Mama Lena, and Asylaion to the mining town. Asylaion becomes mayor, while Basil, Nikephoros, Constans, Ryld, and Theo take leading military and operational roles. Alexander leaves Nova Roma with an overcrowded ship, limited funds, and an independent base. He intends to build western trade and strength before returning to confront the city's rulers.

recaps.ending: Alexander ends the book as emperor of a restored Roman Empire based in Nova Roma, having killed Alexios III and accepted the imperial title along with the Descendant of the Gods evolution. His five bodies are linked again and can trade skills freely. An offered ascension of one body has no stated result. Paris has fallen, its Capetian king is serving a life sentence in a secret prison, and a neutral king of Picardy origin rules France under a binding treaty with Alexander. The Nova Roma Legion has surrendered under contract, the priests are dead, and the Vikings are at peace under the young skald-Jarl. The main Mongol horde is broken and its survivors are paroled, though the remaining Mongol powers may still seek revenge. Genghis Khan's dragon spirit serves Alexander, who has promised to release it after a fair sentence. A century later, Nova Roma is a prosperous city of many species. Alexander's bodies hold separate posts, from the emperor at his desk to an archmage running the Academy and a necromancer under Paris. Constans, his adopted daughter, runs the legion academy. Ivy is an elder dragon, Isabella lives in a homunculus body, and Oliver is head librarian and married to Margot. Giles has a body but has not completed his return to life. Basil and Theo are dead and honored with a statue. Threads left open include the Terracotta Cure, expanding the teleport network, a ceasefire between Egypt and the undead Ottomans, the 42 ancient mysteries, the failing world shield, and the newest body's choice of an expedition to Cahokia, Londinium or Japan.
recaps.in_short: A pre-Cataclysm artifact throws Prime, the Mage and two warring armies onto the Mongolian steppe and cuts Alexander's five bodies off from one another. In the west, the Crafter defends Venice against a pirate armada at the cost of his right hand, then wipes out the pirates. The Monk travels north, has the Viking supreme leader poisoned and killed, and puts a young skald in his place. In the east, Prime takes the city of Khan Jochi IV, breaks through the Great Wall into an empty China whose people have been turned to clay, wakes the First Emperor, and teleports the army west. When the Crafter summons every body to fight the titan Andronicus, the titan dies and nanobots rebuild them all. Killing Genghis Khan, who has become a golden dragon, restores the link between the bodies. Prime's army crosses undead Ottoman Isfahan, destroys a Mongol horde and sails home. Converging allied armies take Paris, the king is convicted, and a new King of France is crowned. The army then takes Sofia, bombards Nova Roma, and storms the palace with all five bodies. Alexander kills Emperor Alexios III and becomes emperor. A century later the empire is thriving, and his newest body is about to choose an expedition.

recaps.text: Previously: Alexander is one mind living in five bodies. Prime is a warrior who rides the shadow dragon Ivy. The Mage has been posing as William, a student, among the mages of Chartres and Paris, alongside his friend Oliver. The Monk runs a Paris criminal gang called the Lost Legion. The Crafter is a gunsmith and enchanter, and the newly created Necromancer is still at the very start of its class. Alexander has killed the Egyptian sun god and a titan, built up holdings that include the town of Lakeside, and gained a number of bound spirits. These include Isabella, a betrayed former innkeeper who became the Shadow Queen, and Giles, a ghost who was once a leading Paris mage and who was promised the chance to research a way back to life. His legion is commanded by Basil. Constans, an ogre commander, now leads his forces at sea. With an alliance of French kings and the support of Margot's family in Normandy, he has been at war with the crown of Paris. The Paris king compelled an Indian professor of pre-Cataclysm magic to serve him by holding the professor's family hostage. Paris also faces Viking raids from the north and pirates in the Mediterranean.

So far this book: A status review lists Alexander's five bodies, their classes, his spirits, and his open quests. These include claiming River's End, which requires defeating a sleeping sea titan, and a Doppelganger upgrade that would let his bodies swap skills. A pre-Cataclysm artifact then explodes. Prime and the Mage, along with the allied army and the Parisian army, about 25,000 to 30,000 people in all, wake on a featureless grassland as winter approaches, with no food, tents or fuel. The Parisian marshal is dead. Prime has lost contact with his other three bodies and cannot summon his spirits. He arranges a truce, and the four young officers left in charge of the Parisian force sign a magical contract that puts them under his command. The Mage, still disguised as William, finds the Indian professor unconscious and spares him because he acted to protect his family. The Parisian leaders mistake the Mage for the professor's assistant and put him in charge of the army's mages. Oliver backs him, and he wins a leadership duel against a veteran earth mage. Back in France, the Crafter stands on the empty field by the walled city on the Somme, cut off from Prime and the Mage, while the Monk and Necromancer remain in France and Isabella stays near the Necromancer. A letter from Constans warns that a pirate armada of hundreds of ships is preparing to sail, probably for Venice.

So far this book: On the grassland, Prime and Ivy scout while the armies follow a huge herd south for food and water. Soldiers begin to vanish at night, so Prime has a walled camp built. In the west, the Crafter sends his Stormhawk to order Constans to delay the armada. He organizes the north around the queen of Wallen and Artois, the last original allied monarch still there, and Normandy, now ruled by Margot's father, raises an army. In Venice a second legion is raised, Theo is given command of naval defense, and the defense centers on a captured island. In Paris the Monk takes over the Assassin's Guild, puts bounties on the king and his war party, and plans to free the professor's captive family. During the king's ball, Lost Legion teams led by Julian and Marie free the professor's wife and daughter along with other prisoners. A fairy, Featherlight, exposes a royal spy among the freed hostages and hires the Monk to free her enslaved people. The dwarf king Deepbreaker promises a year of dwarven soldiers. The falcon-headed god of Alexandria can offer only a Nubian mercenary contract, because the gods are at war and an Ottoman lich commander has returned. Mongol coins confirm that the stranded army is in Mongol territory, where everyone in the city bears a forehead glyph. The Mage sees magic lines running from those glyphs to the ruler's yurt, which Prime reads as a possible sign of control or draining. The ruler, Khan Jochi IV, offers the army winter shelter and supplies, but what he wants in return is still unclear.

So far this book: The Monk discovers that Featherlight's enslaved fairies are pets kept in birdcages by schoolgirls in northern Paris. Posing as a royal inspector, he persuades the staff to release them all without harming anyone. In Alexandria, the Crafter hires a Nubian mercenary company that turns out to number 15,000 for a year, and Egypt lends large-hold ships to carry them to Venice. He and Theo race to the island where Constans has been wearing the armada down, and she takes command of an allied fleet of Carthaginian, Venetian and Alexander's own ships. On the first day the fleet sinks or cripples dozens of pirate vessels, but it runs out of ammunition and falls back toward Venice. That night the Crafter flies over the transports and destroys many with explosive bullets and a whirling storm of stored weapons, while Isabella leads the spirits against the rear of the fleet. A stray fireball burns his right side and fuses his hand to his revolver Proteus, and a surgeon amputates the arm below the elbow. The Nubians and about 3,000 dwarven riflemen arrive just before the pirates land in Venice. The pirate admiral's healing war banner keeps her troops going until a monster-killer bullet tears off her arm and she escapes. Dwarven volleys break the assault, the allied fleet closes from behind, and Venice is saved at heavy cost.

So far this book: The Venice victory raises the Mage's High Marshal class, even though he is stranded on the steppe, where he grows crops by magic for the hungry army camped by the Mongol city. The army's mages discover that the night disappearances are the work of stealthy trapdoor-spider monsters, and the Mage upgrades the wards to detect them. The aged leader of the city's spirit mages agrees to trade knowledge with him, but will say only that the brands come from terrible black magic. In Paris the fairies declare their contract fulfilled and pledge to spy for the Monk for the rest of his life. They warn that a sea power named Andronicus is angry with Alexander and is sending Vikings against his shores. The Monk leaves an assassin lieutenant in charge of the Lost Legion under a loyalty contract, introduces the Necromancer to the gang as his cousin, and sets off north toward his city of River's End. The Necromancer stays under Paris and trains with the catacomb necromancers. He raises an enhanced undead crow named Raven and learns that Giles has turned to studying soul residue in search of resurrection. He also secretly copies the key to the Chartres monument stone, makes rubbings of the stone for Lakeside, and uses the monument to start a Multicasting upgrade quest.

So far this book: A month on, the army is starving while the Khan sends only scraps. Basil and a knight commander warn that the soldiers will act on their own, and after a last fruitless appeal Prime decides to take the city. In a night assault the Mage's combined mages keep the shamans out of the fight, and the shaman elder stands aside. Jochi bursts out drawing stolen strength from thousands of branded subjects, and the elder explains that Jochi is a fifth-generation descendant of Genghis Khan, who is still alive and cannot die. The Mage curses Jochi, traps him in ice and shields Ivy, who pins him for hours. Oliver joins with his strengthened summon Marigold, and Prime impales the Khan on his greatsword. At dawn they deface the glyph on Jochi's forehead, which returns the stolen attributes to his people. Jochi is caged, the allied kings take over administration, and underground stores are enough to see the city and army through winter. In Venice, Constans is celebrated for capturing the one-armed pirate commander. The fleet then sails to Sardinia, where the pirate king, who serves an entity known as the Lord of the Great Abyss as its apostle, fights the Crafter in the air. The god merges with its wounded apostle, but a birdlike being the Crafter once freed returns and kills them both. Theo becomes Admiral and Constans gains the Grand Margrave class. Sardinia's ports are wrecked, and Marseille surrenders without a fight.

So far this book: The Monk crosses the northern snow and finds River's End already held by Vikings who broke the landward wall. A regional quest gives him six months to retake it. Disguised as a Viking, he learns that the invaders follow three jarls, some of whom resent the titan's orders. He resolves to sail to the Viking homeland, kill their aging supreme leader, Spine-Chiller, and arrange a friendlier successor. He reaches a hall-town in Norway and, posing as a clanless Swede, accepts a post guarding a cliffside farming settlement until he can find passage east. On the steppe, Prime hunts monsters to strengthen his combat classes while the caged Jochi goes mad under the Mage's curse. Prime and the Mage clear a dungeon flawlessly, which earns a perk that doubles dungeon rewards. The female Mongol guard then confesses that Jochi summoned hordes from two northern cities, each of fifty thousand riders or more, to march in spring. Prime prepares wagons, rations and mobile forges for a retreat home, and accepts her defection on condition of a loyalty contract. In Marseille, the Crafter forges blades to advance his Metal Mind skill and builds a metal arm from orichalcum and Egyptian bronze. Attaching it triggers a transhumanism change that fills his body with healing nanobots and upgrades his gear. He then heads to Venice to build a combined army against the French and the Vikings.

So far this book: Living with a Norwegian farm family, the Monk finds glowing growth runes in the winter fields and copies them for Lakeside. He kills a stealthy sabre-toothed bear and makes its pelt into a stealth cloak, which merges his crafting classes into Master Artificer. A retired Valkyrie and her husband start him on the Valkyrie class quest. He sails on to Sweden, clears a haunted burial mound with a young messenger, and defeats an elder draugr by pulling it into his mindscape, where Isabella commands his defenses. He then reveals his true purpose to the young skald who leads the Wegmunding clan: kill the supreme leader and put the skald in his place. In Paris, the Necromancer's gang cuts off the king's southern messengers, the Lost Legion has made the south of the city prosperous, and the Necromancer studies how to control monsters. He travels to the Gallo-Angevin lands of Geoffrey of Anjou and camps over a dormant nest of bladed insect monsters, planning to take control of them by spring. In the east, the army strips the Mongol city of wagons, horses and food and marches west with the mad Khan as a hostage. Some five hundred Mongols volunteer to join. The Mage gains the Rune Mage class, while the recovered professor helps him but keeps his distance. About 30,000 soldiers now move west under Prime, pursued by a horde.

So far this book: The Monk trains the young skald-Jarl until the Jarl unlocks the Monk of the Pristine Mind class. Together they clear monster dens along a Swedish coast crowded with refugees, and the Monk gains his first Valkyrie levels. In the east, Mongol riders harass the column until Prime reveals the legion's rifles. He arms his Mongol volunteers as revolver-carrying dragoons, then hides troops in dug-out chambers under the camp and springs an ambush that routs the pursuing riders. In the west, the Crafter marches north from Venice with more than twenty thousand troops, including Lynx's Nubian mercenaries, dwarven riflemen and new legionnaires. They pass under the Alps by rail, and Deepbreaker personally brings ten thousand more dwarves. Four Parisian armies are moving north, but the Crafter overrules Constans, who wants to strike at Paris, and goes after the Viking raiders first. At the Vikings' great meeting the young Jarl challenges Spine-Chiller himself. The Monk, helped by Featherlight, has secretly poisoned the leader with a witch's brew. The weakened champion falls, and the Jarl takes the title of supreme leader along with a share of his strength. His first orders call the raiders home from the south, end the raids, and assign warriors to hunt monsters for half of each year. A status review follows, listing every body's progress.

So far this book: Driven south by the horde, the army reaches an enchanted Great Wall of China with no gates, guarded only by thousands of terracotta soldiers and carved maps holding glowing orbs. The cannons break one of the wall's protective runes, and Prime and Ivy lead the assault over the breach. Prime kills a Mongol war leader, and the army crosses at dusk, taking an orb with it. The Mage and the professor talk openly and partly reconcile. Tracing the orb's magic, the Mage finds that it points to the old Silk Road terminus and suspects it is part of a teleport network. Beyond the wall the land is empty. In the first city the army reaches, every inhabitant has been turned to clay, and when one statue breaks the whole city wakes and swarms them. A world quest, the Terracotta Plague, opens. At River's End the Vikings have withdrawn, but one jarl defies the order and raids an allied outpost. The Crafter and Lynx ambush him, and the Crafter executes the jarl as a warning. The Monk signs a trade pact with the new Viking ruler, gains the Regicide skill, and finds River's End retaken, with its former captain freed and made governor. Reaching Nova Roma, the Monk finds Legion troops occupying the dark elf enclave, and a golden-eyed presence blocks the dark elf priestess when she tries to contact Prime.

So far this book: The army takes the terracotta city without losses, loots its stores, and holds a feast that finally merges the two armies into one. In the city's library the Mage reads that Qin Shi Huang built the Great Wall and the first terracotta army, and that no record of his death exists. On the Rhine, the Crafter tracks the half-mile-long sea titan Andronicus and finds that his bullets barely scratch it. When he uses Summon Your Posse, it works for the first time since the separation. It pulls in his spirits, the Monk and the Necromancer, and finally Prime, Ivy and the Mage from China, all of them falling out of the sky above the titan. The Mage freezes the titan in place, the bodies and spirits attack, and the Crafter's nanobots eat it from inside until it dies. The nanobots then rebuild every body, and Ivy, with metal and engineered organs. The summons ends, sending Prime, the Mage and Ivy back east, although a faint mental link now reaches toward them. The Crafter gives the Necromancer the titan's core, which lets him slay and raise thousands of the dormant insect monsters. The Monk captures part of the titan's spirit. The western army gathers at the walled city on the Somme, which the dwarves have fortified, as the Parisian armies close in.

So far this book: In China, Prime learns that Isabella came east with him during the titan summons. The army marches to Chang'an, where a scout team led by the Mage finds a vast teleport map carved beneath the imperial palace. Prime teaches the ogres the Berserker class, and a Mongol war leader invents a Dragoon class that Prime then learns from her. The Mage works out that the map needs a separate controller. He finds it in a fortress of 20,000 clay soldiers, along with a jade dragon that commands the clay army, and takes both. He also secures a hidden vault of treasure under a magical oath of secrecy. Then, with Isabella, he fights through the First Emperor's trapped tomb and wakes the emperor, who is preserved, not clay. In the west, Parisian armies besiege the walled city on the Somme, where Constans holds the south wall and the Crafter raids the besiegers. The Monk joins the titan's spirit to his own, and the Crafter starts nanobot upgrades on himself, with Constans asking to be next. The grieving First Emperor gives the Mage control of the clay army and the secrets of the map. Imperial records show that a cure meant for a plague read the Cataclysm itself as an infection and turned the whole population to clay. The Terracotta Plague quest completes, a Terracotta Cure quest opens, and the army, with 20,000 clay soldiers, teleports to the westernmost node.

So far this book: At a Bulgarian monastery, monks tell the Monk that his link to his other bodies has been severed and will need a powerful catalyst to restore. He gains the Spirit Vessel class and returns to Nova Roma. The army emerges in a plundered clay city and plans a route through Khotan, Kashgar and Samarkand to bring silk-making stock home. Prime invites the four young Parisian leaders to join him, and Isabella explains that she is anchored to his group of bodies. At Khotan, the Mage lures giant silk moths into an ambush by 20,000 terracotta archers. In Nova Roma, the Legion is arresting merchants. The Monk kills the officer running the crackdown and takes his memories, learning that the Legion commander is an ancient, ambitious general who conquered Sofia, and that the emperor means to use the Legion to build his own army. At the Somme siege, the Crafter enhances Constans and Lynx with nanobots, forms an oath-bound personal guard, gains the Bioshaper class, and leaves Constans in command while he marches west to help Normandy. At Osh the army rests and votes for a southern route home. Prime has an Ottoman contact from his time in Egypt, Pasha Yildiz. At Samarkand, buried clay soldiers destroy a charge of 5,000 riders. The Necromancer marches his insect army on Angers, and after three days Geoffrey of Anjou surrenders and is bound to obey.

So far this book: Samarkand is taken without bloodshed, and an enchanted marble block there opens a world quest to uncover forty-two mysteries of the ancient world. The city's Khan stays behind, expecting to be executed. As the army moves on, a huge golden dragon attacks from behind and announces that he is Genghis Khan. Massed cannon fire brings him down, Prime drains his golden blood, and Ivy chokes off his final breath attack so that it bursts inside him. Far away in Normandy, the Crafter receives the kill notices and, suddenly, the memories of Prime and the Mage. All five bodies are linked again, and the Doppelganger upgrade completes, so they can now trade skills freely, with a one-year lock on each moved ability. The dragon's blood also grants a risky time-slowing ability. The Crafter turns down an advance from Lynx because he is seeing someone, and he and Isabella are reunited. The army eats the dragon's meat, and Ivy swallows his core. The Mage finally learns true flight and completes his Multicasting upgrade. Prime, the Mage and Ivy then enter the spirit realm, capture Genghis Khan's spirit, and destroy his human mind, leaving only a bound dragon spirit that they intend to free after a fair sentence.

So far this book: Another Mongol horde follows the army through the mountains to a vast chasm filled with stitched undead. Beyond it lies Isfahan, a city of undead Ottomans living ordinary lives, whose three-member council must agree before the crossing can open. After proving he is no Egyptian spy, Prime offers to broker peace with Egypt and sends word to Pasha Yildiz. In Normandy, the Crafter's raids cost the Parisian field army nearly a third of its men. When it turns back, the Necromancer's undead block its path, and with Normandy's forces surrounding it, the army surrenders and its soldiers go home under twenty-year parole contracts. The king of Normandy retakes his capital. On the steppe, the Mage parleys with the horde's elders under a truth contract that removes a thousand riders from any battle for each honest answer. He admits that Genghis Khan is dead and hands over the shattered Jochi. Pasha Yildiz arrives with elite undead and overrules the hostile skeleton councillor. The roughly fifty-thousand-strong horde charges into pits, rune mines and cannon fire and is surrounded by terracotta soldiers and Isfahan's undead, while the bound golden dragon wipes out its rear. The survivors are paroled and disarmed, and the skeleton councillor is soon killed by two dark elves. After meeting the undead Sultan, who wants a trade treaty, Prime sails from Antioch on Theo's fleet to winter in Marseille.

So far this book: The Monk spends the winter scouting Nova Roma. The priests' temples hold a dark power even the fairies avoid, the Legion commander plans slave raids and a western conquest, and Emperor Alexios III, paranoid and heavily guarded, plans to abandon the city with his nobles. Wintering in Marseille, Prime pays the army from the Chinese treasure. His clay soldiers take Toulouse in a single night, and Genghis Khan's dragon spirit breaks the walls of Bordeaux, leaving Paris isolated. In Venice, the Mage builds a working teleport prototype keyed to gold coins and linked to the Carthage map. The Crafter shows Constans the secret of the Egyptian linked holds and forges a titan-bone scythe for the Necromancer. The siege of the walled city on the Somme ends when clay soldiers and undead rise from the snow around the starving besiegers, whose general surrenders. It emerges that the Paris king was the one who used the broken orb on Alexander's army. Under Paris, Giles has found a way to live for four to six weeks in a stitched body, and the Necromancer offers Isabella a gift tied to that research. Allied armies close in on Paris from every side, and the professor departs to rejoin his family, with trust only partly restored. The king refuses terms, and a purple barrier withstands the opening bombardment.

So far this book: The Mage unleashes the raw power of his titan core and, together with Ivy and the golden dragon spirit, shatters the barrier and blows open the southern wall. Ogres and goblins pour through, undead guided by the Lost Legion rise inside the city, and allied armies attack from all four sides, with Constans and Deepbreaker leading in the north. Oliver fights beside Margot and her father. The south falls quickly, partly because of discontent with the king. Prime is stopped at the Seine until the earth mage, now a loyal ally, raises a stone bridge from a manor wall for the ogres to cross. The Mage freezes most of the eastern city and, with Isabella's spirits, hunts down the Paris college mages in their redoubts. The Necromancer leads an underground attack on the reserves in the north, and two crossbow sisters on the rooftops cut off the call for reinforcements. The captured king is tried in a hall built under Charlemagne, with Lothair, an allied queen and Venice's representative as judges. Witnesses include the professor's wife, King Francis, and Giles, who admits that he led raids on thirty-seven Rhine outposts on the king's orders. After seven days the king is found guilty and sentenced to life imprisonment in an undisclosed place. Alexander declares that the law will now bind nobles and commoners alike.

So far this book: Two months later the deposed king is taken away in secret, and a neutral king of Picardy origin is sworn in as king of France. He signs a binding treaty with Alexander and promises help against Nova Roma. Settler teams go out to Gibraltar, an island south of Sicily, and Cyprus, and new teleport links are made to a cavern beneath Nova Roma and to a Bulgarian monastery. The army takes Sofia from a Legion garrison and arrives at Nova Roma in early summer alongside Theo's warships. Naval guns smash the Patriarch's enclave, its shield and its temples, deliberately leaving the priests exposed to the city's monsters. The merchants' enclave falls, and constant night bombardment draws monsters onto the priests and the Legion. The priests are killed in their temples, and after a week the Legion withdraws in good order to its castle. Its commander surrenders under a contract never to take up arms against Alexander, and Constans leads the defense of the walls through the night. Deepbreaker goes home but leaves his troops. All five bodies then storm the palace, where an old Varangian guard steps aside. Alexios III's reversal magic briefly kills Prime, who is revived, and Prime then tears through the emperor's armor and kills him. Alexander accepts the imperial title, gains the Descendant of the Gods evolution, and is hailed as emperor while Constans kneels in tears.

Through the end: In the first epilogue, a lizardfolk warrior king leads thousands of his people through a shaman-made portal that opens in central Russia. A black-winged armored commander speaks to him, and the waiting Roman cannons and rifles kill the king and his entire army, showing that the new empire can move troops to portal sites and defeat invaders from other worlds. The second epilogue jumps a century ahead. Nova Roma is a prosperous magical city of many species, crossed by trams. Alexander's bodies each have their own post: the emperor does paperwork, the archmage runs the Nova Roma Academy, the monk teaches where the priests once lived, the crafter works in Lakeside, and others live as a Viking in the north, a pirate on a Cyprus-based warship, and a necromancer under Paris. Constans, now the emperor's adopted daughter, runs the legion academy. Ivy has grown into an elder dragon. Oliver is head librarian of the Grand Library and married to Margot, heir to Normandy. Giles wears a body and has more freedom but is still working toward full rebirth. Basil and Theo have died and are honored with a statue. A newly made Alexander body visits the Explorer's Guild, chartered in the thirty-first year of Emperor Alexander I, and is met there by Isabella in a homunculus body. The book closes as he must choose an expedition to Cahokia, Londinium or Japan.

characters.description: The narrator: a single mind running several doppelganger bodies, each with its own class and gear. His prime body is a warrior with a bonded shadow-dragon mount, shadow armor and a Spirit Breaker class that captures spirits; a monk body carries psychic and shadow skills and a shape-shifting dagger; a crafter body works as gunsmith, enchanter and blacksmith; and a mage body, an Ascendant Elementalist, is about to enroll at a Paris school. He already governs two territories, has slain a titan, a giant king and a green dragon, and has open quests to claim Emisa and River's End and to defeat the sleeping titan Andronicus.
characters.name: Alexander

characters.description: A spirit bound to Alexander's service. In life he ranked among the best graduates of the Paris magic schools, trained in all four elements and in esoteric magic, and he swore service to the Paris crown in exchange for a powerful class. He broke that oath, unwillingly, to become a spirit companion, on the promise that he would be free to look for a way back to life and to take revenge on the man who killed him.
characters.name: Giles

characters.description: One of the spirits Alexander has captured: a necromancer queen who is half elf and half spider and wields deathfrost magic. She is cursed, was driven into exile, and is unstable in mind.
characters.name: The Deathfrost Monarch

characters.description: A lightning stormhawk, one of the spirits Alexander has captured through his prime body's Spirit Breaker class.
characters.name: The stormhawk

characters.description: A dark spirit and close friend of Alexander. Before his monk body moves into the Paris underworld, she spends time scouting the gangs of the poorer southern bank and picks out the failing gang he approaches with his offer.
characters.name: Isabella

characters.description: Two crossbow-armed women in the small, struggling gang on the southern bank of Paris that Alexander's monk body approaches with an offer to lead.
characters.name: The crossbow women

characters.description: Leader of the small, struggling gang on the southern bank of Paris that Alexander's monk body offers to lead. He fights with daggers, wears a gold tooth, and is doubtful of the stranger's promises while wanting to believe them. Once the gang agrees, his group breaks into the rival smuggler's guardhouse base.
characters.name: Julian

characters.description: A large, mace-wielding woman in the southern Paris gang that Alexander takes over, and its clearest-headed and most dependable member. In the move against the rival enforcer, she commands the second team waiting behind his fortified villa.
characters.name: Marie

characters.description: Bookkeeper for the rival Paris gang known as the nine men. Alexander's monk body slips into his bedroom using Shadow Jump and stealth and carries him off as a captive as the gang moves against its other leaders.
characters.name: The bookkeeper

characters.description: A stocky orphan who worked in the Chartres library before enrolling as a first-year. He earned a unique mage class, Libra Master, which lets him draw on books to summon things out of stories. Shy and eager, he befriends Alexander's mage body and lodges on the top floor of the residence hall with the low-ranked students.
characters.name: Oliver

characters.description: An older first-year at Chartres, in her twenties, who at first is rude to Oliver and Alexander and mutters insults in class. She comes along on Oliver's library tour after a confrontation and gives her name. Her father was a count who lost his region to a Normandy king allied with Paris, and she studies at Chartres hoping that serving the king will win her family's land back. She begins to warm to the two of them.
characters.name: Margot

characters.description: The professor of pre-Cataclysm magic at Chartres. Born in India, he came from a distant college to teach in Paris. His course covers sympathetic magic, in which spells are tied to natural or cultural associations.
characters.name: Pre-Cataclysm magic professor

characters.description: Alexander's dragon companion, who shares attributes with him and leads the legion's young dragon wyrmlings. In the spring campaign against the Ogre Kingdom, her wyrmlings strike alongside the cavalry and goblins to help break the ogre charge.
characters.name: Ivy

characters.description: One of the leaders of Alexander's legion. He commands legionnaires at the defensive wall during the spring campaign against the raiding Ogre Kingdom.
characters.name: Basil

characters.description: A female ogre who serves as one of the leaders of Alexander's legion. In the battle against the Ogre King's army she stands at the barricade and calls the rifle volleys.
characters.name: Constans

characters.description: Ruler of the Ogre Kingdom to the east of Alexander's Rhine territory, whose people raided the legion's outposts. A huge warrior with a giant club, he leads about three hundred warriors and an Ogre Mage against the legion and is brought down when cannon, rifles, cavalry and dragons break his charge.
characters.name: The Ogre King

characters.description: A female ogre spellcaster who marches with the Ogre King against Alexander's legion, fighting with a rune staff and shields.
characters.name: The Ogre Mage

characters.description: A ruler who styles himself king of an eastern Frankish kingdom and writes from Lyon. He is Alexander's newest ally and asks for help because a Parisian army is said to be marching east to punish him.
characters.name: Francis

characters.description: A loud noble student at Chartres. When the year-one results put Alexander's student identity first in four classes, he objects in front of the dining hall and leads the resentment against the rankings.
characters.name: Armand

characters.description: An elf ally of Alexander who works as his spymaster. He has been keeping watch on Francis's commanders and has sent agents into Wallen and Artois. After Lyon falls, Alexander sends him to look into elves working at a Lyon brothel and offer them help.
characters.name: Elf spymaster

characters.description: King of Lorraine, one of the regional rulers Francis writes to, at Alexander's direction, about renewing the eastern alliance. Francis speaks of him as self-important.
characters.name: Lothair

characters.description: A wealthy, charming noble student at Chartres who places first in manners. He invites Alexander to join his dungeon team and is turned down, and he proves more politically decent than Alexander expected.
characters.name: Philip, Count of Valois

characters.description: A young assistant professor at Chartres who escorts Alexander down to the monument beneath the main hall to claim his skill upgrades. He offers himself as a useful connection, and Alexander makes a note of his name and residence.
characters.name: Michel de Bellrose

characters.description: A large bear spirit in Alexander's service whose aura spreads disease. The monk body calls him up with the other spirits to tear apart a base of the Sinholders, the gang that holds the Paris river.
characters.name: Kermode

characters.description: The older of the two leaders of the Sinholders, the gang controlling the Paris river, with a strong stealth skill. During Alexander's raid he wounds Giles, but loses the fight, surrenders under a twenty-four-hour contract and gives up his rare Assassin class. He tells Alexander that the gang's other leader, his former wife, has to be killed.
characters.name: The older Sinholder boss

characters.description: Co-leader of the Sinholders gang and former wife of the boss Alexander captured. When Julian and Marie raid her hideout she escapes through a hidden tunnel, and anti-scrying magic keeps even Isabella from finding her.
characters.name: The Sinholder leader

characters.description: King of Burgundy: blunt, loud and eager for a fight. He arrives at Lyon with about two thousand spearmen and four hundred crossbowmen, backs Alexander after learning of Francis's surrender, and explains that pirates and monsters at home keep him from sending more troops.
characters.name: Reynold

characters.description: Ruler of Wallen, who is not at the Lyon feast. The visiting kings describe her as independent, shaped by Celtic tradition and feared for her curses. She dislikes both Paris and Artois, and her husband has recently died.
characters.name: Queen of Wallen

characters.description: An older, bald, good-natured captain whose trade ship, belonging to an Egyptian empire said to be ruled by gods, is captured by Alexander's blockade. He explains that trade requires pleading before a god in Alexandria. Alexander lets him go on condition that he comes back to guide him there.
characters.name: The Egyptian captain

characters.description: A big, loud, bearded knight from Champenois in full plate. An old friend who met Alexander near Nova Roma and first introduced him to King Francis, he is appointed war commander of the Lyon army. Alexander tells him the whole truth, including that Francis is effectively his vassal, and the knight is amused and stays loyal.
characters.name: The Champenois knight

characters.description: Two sisters, both expert shots with enchanted crossbows, who act as bodyguards to Alexander's monk body in the Paris gang. The monk has handed his Assassin class on to them. When assassins struck at the monk and Isabella after dinner, one sister was taken and then freed by the monk, and both came close to dying while defending the pair. Once he recovers, they go on guarding him in good spirits.
characters.name: The Chappelle sisters

characters.description: A being with a man's body and a living falcon's head who sits enthroned inside Alexandria's gold-capped pyramid. His crier proclaims him lord of the sky, sun, moon, healing, protection and kings. Alexander is brought before him to ask for trade rights.
characters.name: Falcon-headed god of Alexandria

characters.description: Wife of the Egyptian captain. She recognises the name Constantinople and asks about the Ottomans, with whom Egypt has been at war for about seventy years. While her husband is away she warns Alexander and Constans to leave before they are caught in a war between gods, and hands Alexander a note arranging a meeting the next night.
characters.name: Zara

characters.description: A cat-headed goddess in a white toga, linked to the sun and to protection, who meets Alexander and Constans in secret at her Alexandria temple. Weak and peaceful, she trades in information. She explains that Egypt's gods chose mortal bodies over sacrificing themselves for the world's shield, which is now fading, and that her faction wants kingship given back to humans with gods as advisers.
characters.name: Bastet

characters.description: The old, stubborn and shrewd king of Picardy, proud of his Gaulish descent. He gathers about eight thousand troops at his capital and uses marshland, pikemen and castle artillery to neutralize the allied knights. At the parley he refuses to join the alliance, arguing that Paris would not stop at the south.
characters.name: The Picardy king

characters.description: A falcon-headed sun god who rules Memphis, attended by a floating disc of sunlight and guarded by priests and soldiers. A former pharaoh-god who seized his place, he can turn his guards golden, animate great statues and renew a sun shield through prayer. Alexander's crafter body ambushes him at a morning ceremony at his temple, and after a battle involving all of Alexander's bodies and spirits, kills him.
characters.name: Falcon-headed sun god of Memphis

characters.description: A skeletal mage with a huge turban and a face animated by illusion, who rules the orderly undead town inside a wild dungeon in Egypt's Western Desert and judges its disputes under the title of Pasha. Shocked to meet a living human, he tells Alexander that he built the dungeon himself and had long expected an outsider to find its entrance.
characters.name: The Pasha

characters.description: Margot's father, a former count forced off his lands, now living in Paris. He insists on meeting at the king's gala rather than privately. On a palace balcony, Alexander's monk body offers him the throne of Normandy.
characters.name: Margot's father

characters.description: The Capetian ruler of Paris, seen for the first time at his own ball: short, thinning curly brown hair, plain clothes and a fit build. He announces that two armies will go against rebellious eastern lords, that a larger new army will be raised in Paris, and that soldiers are being called up. Alexander judges him shrewd and politically able.
characters.name: The King of Paris

characters.description: A Parisian commander at the head of a large army moving north toward the Picardy king's city, while a separate force of knights and light cavalry heads for Lyon.
characters.name: Philip II

characters.description: Twenty automaton mages created by Alexander, who arrive at Lyon by caravan with their leaders, guarded by undead Parisian elite fighters that his armor raised. One leader speaks psychically and calls Alexander father, another is female, and a third stays at the mithril mine to build more of them. Alexander tells them to protect one another first and the city second.
characters.name: The Verum

characters.description: A strict necromancer with glowing blue eyes who works in the tunnels beneath Paris. He takes on Alexander's new necromancer body and the spirit Giles as students, and threatens them when annoyed.
characters.name: The necromancer mentor

characters.description: A tattooed, scarred ring fighter from the southern Paris slums, conscripted into the amateur mage unit that Alexander's student body is given to lead at the Orleans camp. He threatens Alexander on arrival and is put on the ground with a punch and a throw.
characters.name: The pit-fighter

characters.description: Commander of the Parisian army marching north: large, hairy, talkative and overbearing. Alexander's student body dines with him on the march and judges him a second choice, since Philip II is a prisoner at Lakeside.
characters.name: The Parisian marshal

recaps.ending: The last battle never happens as planned. Inside the Parisian camp, the mage body, still posing as the student William, learns that the pre-Cataclysm professor has been ordered by the King of Paris to throw a broken Roman transport orb into the allied army, because the king holds the professor's wife and daughter. The mage kills the Parisian marshal, but the professor launches the orb. Prime and Ivy fail to catch it, and the crafter shatters it from about two miles away with a monster-killer bullet. No portal opens; instead about thirty thousand soldiers from both armies disappear from the field. Prime wakes with Ivy beside both armies, all alive, on an endless golden grassland with no city, walls or camp in sight, and suspects they may no longer be in their own world. He fears a new Parisian leader could restart the fighting. The crafter is left alone on the city walls. What became of the mage, Oliver, the conscript unit and the professor is left unresolved. The monk still runs the Lost Legion in Paris, where the gang war is largely over and the Sinholder leader is dead. The necromancer body and Giles are studying under the Paris necromancers, with Giles's return to life not yet achieved. Constans holds Venice's fleet and plans deeper raids on the pirates, while Philip II is a prisoner at Lakeside and the King of Paris refuses all terms. The alliance of eastern kings, now including Picardy and Margot's father as king of Normandy, still stands. Open threads include the fading world shield and Egypt's warring gods, the Pasha's fate, the Viking worm titan and the sleeping titan Andronicus, the Nova Roma emperor's conquest of Bulgaria, and Isabella's hope of living again.
recaps.in_short: Alexander, one mind spread across several doppelganger bodies, works against Paris on every front at once. His mage body enrolls undercover at Chartres Academy, sets a dungeon record, befriends Oliver and Margot, and learns to cast through Roman runes. His monk body turns a failing southern gang into the Lost Legion and wins a gang war against the Sinholders and the miners' guild. His prime body humbles King Francis at Lyon, forges an alliance of eastern French kings, wins in Artois and Picardy, and puts Margot's father on the throne of Normandy. His crafter body opens trade with Egypt, kills a falcon-headed sun god as the price of cutting off Egypt's aid to the pirates, and survives a long stay in an Ottoman undead dungeon, emerging with monster-killer bullets and metal wings. As Paris fights back, Lyon holds and Philip II is captured, a new necromancer body enters the Paris underground with Giles, and the mage is drafted into the Parisian army. At the decisive battle the mage kills the Parisian marshal, but the professor throws a broken transport orb; when the crafter shoots it apart, about thirty thousand soldiers of both armies vanish, and Prime wakes with them on an unknown golden plain.

recaps.text: So far this book: Alexander is one mind operating several doppelganger bodies, each with a separate class: a warrior prime body with a shadow-dragon mount, a monk with psychic and shadow skills, a gun-making crafter, and a mage. He already governs two territories and has open quests to claim Emisa and River's End and to stop the sleeping titan Andronicus. The mage body, made small and young, is sworn in at Chartres Academy in Paris under a cover story arranged with Giles, a former Chartres student whom Alexander killed at the Rhine and now keeps as a resentful spirit. Students count as minor nobles and military officers, which worries Alexander, since another of his bodies is in open conflict with Paris. Skipping orientation, he enters the Dungeon of the Ancestors and smashes its elemental statues. When six ghostly archmages refuse him their blessing, he releases power from his titan core, wiping them out and wrecking much of the pocket city while badly injuring himself. He clears the dungeon in record time and wins gold cores, a perk, the title First among equals, access to a hidden archmage study and the Mana Shield skill. Meanwhile the monk body, following Isabella's scouting, enters a failing gang's cellar on the poorer southern bank and offers to help them take Paris. With the gang's leader Julian and the mace fighter Marie, he takes apart the larger rival called the nine men: he kidnaps their bookkeeper, kills the smuggling boss and gives his orichalcum crossbow to two crossbow women, then storms the enforcer's villa without losing a single member. He strips the enforcer's mind of secrets, kills him, and takes over the rival territory and its wealth.

So far this book: A scoreboard at dinner lists the dungeon record under Alexander's real name; because he enrolled under a false noble name, nobody links it to the small newcomer, and suspicion falls on a count's son and the older first-years. He befriends Oliver, an orphan former library worker with the unique summoning class Libra Master, and the prickly older student Margot, whose father lost his county to a Normandy king allied with Paris. The three form a loose study group. Classes begin, and the mage, now level 18, takes advanced mana manipulation and a water focus in the hope of taming his all-or-nothing casting. He learns that the top student in each class may use the college monument to upgrade a skill, and wants to copy that ability for his own cities. He forces Giles into nightly tutoring, pointing to the archmage study as a possible route to the cure Giles was promised. In the east, Prime leads a legion of over a thousand, with cavalry, goblins, fifty dwarven cannons, dark elf scouts and Ivy's wyrmlings, against the raiding Ogre Kingdom, with Basil and the ogre Constans among his leaders. Ogre towns surrender, and a prepared ditch, barricade and cannon line shatter the Ogre King's charge. The King happily accepts terms binding most of his warriors to at least ten years as legion auxiliaries, and everyone present earns the Ogre Endurance perk. The crafter body fortifies River's End with an enchanted seawall against a titan stirring in the North Sea, funds inventors at Lakeside whose linked tomes can pass numbers between books, and plans the Great Bank of Venice alongside a legal code granting equal protection to all adults.

So far this book: Prime brings more than 250 ogres back to Lakeside, where the blacksmith resents the armor order. A letter arrives from King Francis in Lyon, Alexander's newest ally, asking for help against a Parisian army marching east. Prime warns his cities and decides to show the French his legion's real strength. The crafter, sailing with Constans aboard Venice's first warship, a ship of the line with fifty cannons and protective enchantments, sinks three pirate ships, and Constans hands the survivors to Carthage for trial. Prime's legion digs in north of Lyon, the ogres now in enchanted armor, with Ivy and the goblins hidden in the hills. Francis, whose eastern alliance holds less than a third of France, wants the legion only as a reserve. When about five thousand well-equipped Parisians arrive, Francis stages a losing battle and parleys. Prime lands uninvited and names himself Alexander of Constantinople, leader of New Rome, before a calm Parisian marshal who serves the King of Paris. Francis surrenders, agreeing to dissolve his alliance, pay tribute and send foreign armies away within a week, which also ends his contract with Alexander. The legion withdraws, receives full plate for the ogres, and learns that the Parisians have gone home and Francis has disbanded most of his troops. Prime marches back by night, breaches Lyon's walls with cannon fire in about two hours, and sends the armored ogres and Ivy's wyrmlings through the gap. Francis's soldiers flee, and when Prime and Ivy appear at his castle balcony, Francis faints.

So far this book: The year-one exams end with the mage, enrolled as William de Hauteville, first in four classes despite failing mana manipulation and manners. Armand leads the protests, Margot defends him loudly, and rumors spread that she cheated. Alexander takes Oliver and Margot to celebrate at The Emperor's Rest, an inn he secretly owns, escorted by his gang, now the Lost Legion. In Lyon, Prime spares Francis in exchange for a binding contract: Francis funds an army under commanders Alexander chooses, opens trade, hosts a Bank of Venice branch and gives up the Rhine towns. At Alexander's direction he writes to Lorraine, Burgundy, Wallen and Artois, asking their rulers to renew the alliance. At Chartres the mage receives four monument upgrades and assigns one to each body, including a Mana Shield quest and a monthly transfer of skills between bodies, and secretly memorizes the monument's glyphs. The monk turns on the Sinholders, the gang holding the river. With Kermode, Giles, the Deathfrost Monarch and the stormhawk he wrecks one base, beats its older boss and takes his Assassin class. The boss joins him and is given the class back, but his former wife, the other leader, escapes Julian and Marie's raid through a hidden tunnel. Isabella reminds Alexander that a water nymph's blessing lets her live one day each year, and that day is close. Lothair, ruler of Lorraine, and Burgundy's king Reynold reach Lyon with troops, accept Alexander's leadership, and agree to visit the queen of Wallen next. At sea, the crafter's blockade sinks about twenty pirate ships. He declares himself a noble of old Rome's lands and releases an Egyptian captain on condition that he return to guide him to Alexandria.

So far this book: In pre-Cataclysm magic the mage starts a term project to craft a new magic item, while Armand's group keeps trying to provoke him, Oliver and Margot into a fight. In the archmages' study he finds the old Roman method of tracing runes in the air and filling them with mana. After letting dungeon statues pound his shield to complete its upgrade, he casts his first controlled rune beam. Prime leaves his legion to head north, appoints his old friend the Champenois knight commander of Lyon's army, and travels with the three kings to the queen of Wallen, who commits four thousand troops in hope of claiming the northern kingdom. In Paris, Isabella spends her one living day with the monk and the mage. That night assassins attack; the monk takes poisoned bolts aimed at her, and the mage arrives and kills the attackers with rune spells before the monk collapses. A healer keeps him alive but knows of no cure for the venom. Told that the missing Sinholder leader has found shelter with the miners' guild, which mines the king's orichalcum, the mage seals one of its guildhalls in ice and collapses it, killing everyone inside. The allied army, about fifteen thousand strong, marches west. After a local noble's militia is cut down in a skirmish, the legion takes his town overnight and the dwarven cannons level his manor in one volley, shocking the kings. Alexander refuses to share the cannons with the queen. The army reaches the northern king's old Roman fortress city, and the battle begins with the knight leading the line and Prime fighting at the front.

So far this book: In Artois, the allied cannons hold fire until the enemy cavalry advances, then break the ranks. A charge including the ogres follows, with Prime flying beside the knight commander as his guard. The Artois army is routed with few allied losses, Prime gains the legendary High Marshal class, and the queen captures the Artois king to force his abdication and merge his realm with hers. The monk wakes from his coma, reassured by Isabella. His bodyguards, the Chappelle sisters, nearly died protecting them. He passes off the mage who destroyed the guildhall as a reclusive relative and commits the Lost Legion to wiping out the miners' guild. At sea, two more warships arrive, Constans becomes admiral, and Alexander claims an empty island as a patrol base. Following the Egyptian captain, he learns that the Sardinian pirates are trading loot for Egyptian food, and hears of a great awakening a century ago when gods took power. Alexandria proves far larger than Paris, with a gold-capped pyramid and a mage college, and the ship is held until a god approves the visit. A falcon-headed god receives Alexander's trade petition in silence. At dinner the captain's wife Zara reveals that Egypt has warred with the Ottomans for some seventy years and privately warns Alexander and Constans to leave before a war between gods engulfs them. In Paris the assassin trains the monk in burglary, raising his thief class, and guild contracts level his assassin class. At Chartres the mage chooses the Archmage's Vision, an eye artifact, as his project. He has the monk ambush Armand's gang in an alley and break Armand's fingers, levels by clearing the college's other two dungeons, and finishes a ritual fusing five eyes into one artifact, ready to replace his own eye.

So far this book: In a secret meeting at her temple, the cat-headed goddess Bastet tells Alexander and Constans that Egypt's gods chose mortal bodies rather than sacrificing themselves for the world's shield, which is now fading. The gods are splitting into factions, and by petitioning the falcon-headed god Alexander has unknowingly joined his side. Armed men later ambush the pair in the streets, and they kill every one so no word of the guns spreads. The falcon-headed god grants the trade deal, giving Venice a compound in Alexandria and protections for its ships. In a private audience he admits Egypt feeds the pirates and is pledged to defend them, then offers to cut them off if Alexander kills a god for him. In the north, Prime stores battlefield blood for a ring to boost his blood magic, and the army moves on Picardy, whose old king blunts the allied knights with marsh, pikes and castle guns and refuses to join the alliance. In the battle, the stormhawk spots an illusion hiding elite Parisian knights. Prime grows huge on stolen attributes, summons his spirits, and with the ogres, the cavalry and Ivy's dragons destroys the knights, though the legion takes losses. The cannons bring down the castle, the pike line collapses, and a captured knight claims to be a Parisian noble. The captive Picardy king says he sided with Paris as the lesser evil and claims about ninety years of command. Alexander offers him leadership of the alliance's army. In Paris, the monk's gang has picked off the miners' guild foremen one by one; he walks into their underground hall alone and forces the last seven to sign a one-sided truce contract.

So far this book: The crafter shoots the falcon-headed sun god of Memphis from a rooftop at his morning ceremony, wounding but not killing him. The god turns his guards golden and wakes a colossus and the sphinx, and Alexander summons all his bodies, Ivy and his spirits. Darkness bullets and the mage's ice walls cut the god off from sunlight, breaking his shield, and a final bullet kills him. Alexander gains the boon Beloved of the Sun for all his bodies, an attribute reward he puts into leadership, the God-Killer achievement and a choice of divine evolutions. With the river blockaded and his recall stone cracked, he flees into the desert, chased for two days by soldiers, priests in flying chariots and stone sphinxes. Sheltering in a cave with his spirits, he enters a wild dungeon where time runs much faster than outside, leaving Isabella and the others on guard. Inside he finds a sunlit valley where an undead town fights off barbarians, goblins and trolls. At Chartres the mage again tops four classes, Armand's family's assassination contract is refused by the guild, and he picks new upgrades, one of which grants him an extra doppelganger. In the north, Prime learns the exclusive Royal Knight class from a captured Parisian knight and shares it, making Ivy his royal steed. A Viking raid on River's End is beaten off, and the Picardy king explains that the Vikings worship an undersea worm titan. Prime offers him the crown of a reunited Frankish kingdom if he leads the conquest of Paris.

So far this book: After a week of scouting the dungeon, the crafter chooses the True Archmage evolution, which rewards mastery of pre-system magic traditions. He enters the undead town and meets its ruler, a skeletal mage called the Pasha, who says he made the dungeon. The Pasha explains that he is an Ottoman commander about seven hundred years old who saw the siege of Constantinople, where Roman priests unleashed an undead plague that his people survived only by preserving their minds in undeath. Weakened by the desert, he carved off part of his power to build the dungeon as a refuge, but because no one has completed it, it now drains him and sends constant attacks. He welcomes Alexander as an ally. Prime formally brings the Picardy king into the alliance under a loyalty contract; the kings agree to raise new forces while the legion strikes west, starting with Normandy. In southern Paris the gang war is largely over, and a gang member has killed the Sinholder leader in the tunnels. At Chartres, Margot's father agrees to meet only at the king's gala on the island in the Seine. The monk blackmails his way into the gala, evolves his thief class into Crime Lord, and on a balcony offers Margot's father the throne of Normandy. Sorbonne students hold a first-year duel tournament in which losers must teach their class to the winner. The mage wins quietly with shield tricks and rune spells, while Oliver wins acclaim by summoning a queen and a knight from books. In the final, the mage turns Oliver's summons against him and then concedes so Oliver can win a new class.

So far this book: The crafter agrees to defend the Pasha's town in return for a home and workshop, planning for them to leave together after about a year of dungeon time. Over roughly a year and a half inside, he invents the monster-killer bullet, an adamant core with an orichalcum jacket and fourth-dimensional runes that passes through bodies and barriers, and builds metal wings that undead fleshcrafters weave into his back. Once bonded, the wings let him bomb the barbarian hordes. He kills a barbarian blacksmith, clears the caves and defeats the final boss, a half-troll woman with a book of curses, earning the Book of Curses, which he passes to the mage, and the perk Late Bloomer. He then flies out toward Alexandria. In the north, Prime marches into Normandy. Margot's father has accepted his offer and is coming north with Swiss mercenaries. Scouts locate the king of Normandy, Ivy crashes through his manor roof at night, and the king surrenders immediately. Prime finishes his blood ring in the captured manor and installs Margot's father as a contract-bound king of Normandy, required to recall Norman troops from Paris, in a nearly bloodless takeover. In Paris, the King of Paris appears at his ball and announces two armies against the eastern lords and a larger new army. The monk's gang, which now holds the river and the main ore mine under Paris, plans to stop selling orichalcum to the king and ship it to Lyon instead.
